assignment: MMIP Week 07 - Assignment 1: Downstream Tasks and Structured Output Specification

router.product_inquiry: Product features, specifications, usage instructions, and product information
router.customer_support: Product malfunctions, technical issues, customer complaints, compliments, and feedback
router.out_of_scope: Questions unrelated to the company's products or services
router.place_order: Purchasing products, adding items to cart, placing orders, and canceling orders

router.clarification: Cannot determine the user's intent; further information is required

route.description: Downstream task or special handling route

intent.description: Specific user intent; use unknown when it cannot be identified

confidence.description: The classification model's confidence estimate, which may not be a calibrated probability

extracted_slots.description: Extract from the current message and prior context; use null when unavailable and never fabricate values.

missing_slots.description: Required information missing from an otherwise identified intent

response_generation_spec.description: All routes share one Response Generator. The Task Controller selects the template and injects validated variables. The input_schema and output_schema below are formal structural specifications; examples are illustrations.

template_id.description: Selected by the Task Controller; Qwen supplies answer when generating answers; must correspond to an entry in response_templates

template_variables.description: Template placeholder values must be known and validated; never invent database lookup results

conversation_finished.description: Whether the current customer service task is complete, not merely whether this turn has been answered

rules: All responses must be polite and empathetic, in English (en).
All products are assumed in stock; shipping is free; purchase quantities are unlimited. These are simulated classroom policies, not verified database results.
Before purchasing, product_name, quantity, and delivery_address must be provided and the customer must explicitly confirm the order; simulate a successful order only after affirmative confirmation.

Both order tracking and return requests require order_id. After receiving it, apply the fixed policies: delivery within 3 business days; accept all returns, instruct the customer to follow the website's return procedure, and issue a simulated refund within 7 business days.
When human assistance is requested, output only "Transferring to customer service"; do not claim an actual transfer was initiated.

After completing the tasks, ask "Is there anything else I can help you with?" and keep conversation_finished false. Set it to true only when the customer says no further help is needed or an external timer detects 10 minutes of inactivity.
Support multiple intents: collect required information for every task first, then respond in the order the user introduced the tasks; ask about further assistance only once at the end.
When assembling multiple task responses, remove "Is there anything else I can help you with?" from each individual template and append it only once at the end.

Only the three products in product_catalog are offered. Product specifications may be answered only when recorded under specifications. For unlisted specifications or products not sold, reply "I don't know." Qwen may provide known troubleshooting guidance but must say "I don't know" when uncertain.

To cancel an order, first obtain order_id and explicitly ask the customer to confirm cancellation; simulate cancellation only after affirmative confirmation, and leave the order unchanged if declined.
After a simulated order is confirmed, the Task Controller generates a random simulated order ID from 1 to 1000. Never fabricate an ID before generation or reuse an example ID. Do not display prices.
With multiple routes, first fill the required slots for each task separately, then process tasks in FIFO order. Ask for purchase or cancellation confirmation separately when that task's turn arrives.

routing_principle: Support multiple intents and routes: build a task queue in the order each independent task was first mentioned, preserving task_id and sequence_order. Collect all required slots first. If any task has missing slots or ambiguous intent, ask for clarification without producing final task responses. Once information is complete, process and respond in the original order. Purchases require explicit confirmation when their turn comes before being simulated. Ask whether further assistance is needed only once at the end. An external timer handles the 10-minute timeout. Both placing and canceling orders require secondary confirmation, while preserving FIFO order.

multi_router_output_spec.description: For multiple intents, the Router outputs a queue ordered by first occurrence. A single intent may use router_output_spec. Collect all required task information before emitting final task responses in order.

route.description: Downstream task or special handling route

intent.description: Specific user intent; use unknown if it cannot be identified

confidence.description: The classification model's confidence estimate, which may not be a calibrated probability

extracted_slots.description: Extract from the current message and prior context; use null when unavailable and never fabricate values.

missing_slots.description: Required information missing from an otherwise identified intent

sequence_order.description: Number tasks by their first mention; do not sort by the fixed route list or confidence score

task_id.description: Stable identifier for a task across turns within the same conversation

tasks.description: Order is determined by first occurrence; sequence_order is 1, 2, 3, etc. Separate tasks using the same route may have different task_id values.

collection_complete.description: All required slots for every task are complete before execution; final order confirmation is handled separately

next_action.description: Ask for missing information first; once complete, process tasks in order; purchases still require confirmation when their turn arrives

multi_route_execution_policy.ordering_basis: Order by when each independent task was first mentioned in the same message or across turns. Never reorder by route name, confidence, or complexity.
multi_route_execution_policy.deduplicate: Merge supplemental information into the existing task_id; create a new task only for a clearly new independent request
multi_route_execution_policy.missing_slot_strategy: Check required slots for every task before executing any. You may ask for missing information for multiple tasks in one message, but identify which task each field belongs to. Do not provide final task answers during collection.
multi_route_execution_policy.clarification_strategy: If an intent is ambiguous, clarify that task before continuing data collection; do not discard other identified tasks
multi_route_execution_policy.execution: After collecting all required data, execute tasks and deliver responses in sequence_order. Explicit authorization for individual tasks (such as purchasing) is still required when their turn arrives. Cancellation also requires a specific confirmation when its turn arrives; do not cancel before confirmation.
multi_route_execution_policy.result_format: Produce one response section per task, concatenate them in order, and ask about further assistance only once at the end
multi_route_execution_policy.failure_handling: If a task fails, explain why and proceed to the next eligible task; do not pretend it succeeded
multi_route_execution_policy.conversation_finished: Set conversation_finished true only after all tasks are resolved and the user declines further help, or an external timer reaches 10 minutes of inactivity
multi_route_execution_policy.notes: If a user adds a task while information is being collected, append it to the queue. If they merely provide details for an existing task, retain its position.

multi_route_response_generation_spec.description: Reuse the shared Response Generator to produce each task response; the Task Controller then assembles them in order. Information-collection questions are not final task responses.
assembly_rules: Concatenate responses strictly by sequence_order, adding paragraph breaks as needed.
Do not repeat "Is there anything else I can help you with?" for individual tasks; append it only once after all task responses.
Never output a successful purchase before explicit confirmation. Ask for confirmation and wait for approval before continuing.
Cancellation also requires confirmation; never claim success before the user explicitly agrees.
